title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability, roles, stop/logprobs, function calls, response formatting
author: Ethan Park
description: Summary: Implement OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity across the Redwood OpenAI compatibility layer: normalize message roles and role coercion rules, support stop sequences and logprobs in both sync and streaming paths, stabilize streaming chunk framing for function/tool calls, and improve response formatting/structured output to match OpenAI behavior. Motivation: customers expect 1:1 behavior with OpenAI Chat Completions for portability and for our SDKs/console to behave identically when migrating. This PR aligns param handling and edge cases (role aliasing, assistant/system role precedence, empty messages) and fixes streaming framing issues that caused truncated tool call payloads under high concurrency. Checklist: - [x] Role normalization (user/system/assistant) + tests - [x] stop sequences considered in streaming and non-streaming generators - [x] logprobs wired through for non-autoregressive scoring and for top_logprobs in completions - [x] streaming framing stabilized (newline-delimited JSON chunks + event boundaries) - [x] function/tool calling: full call payload unified between stream and final response - [x] response formatting: structured output support and content-type hints - [x] SDK updates (python/typescript) for compatibility shims - [x] e2e parity tests added and passing - [x] docs (openai_compat.md) updated with migration notes Migration notes: The OpenAI compatibility shim aims to accept OpenAI-style params and produce the same high-level outputs. We intentionally coerce legacy role names (e.g., "assistant_bot" -> "assistant") and preserve user-provided role metadata in an 'orig_role' field inside the compatibility wrapper when present. Tests & validation: added unit tests for role normalization, stop matching cases including overlapping stops and unicode stops, and logprob alignment tests against the reference scoring harness. Added an end-to-end parity test that runs against hosted inference profiles and the streaming harness. Performance: minor runtime overhead introduced by additional normalization (~1-2% per-request CPU in microbenchmarks) but batching and kernel selection unaffected. Rolling approach: feature gate enabled by default for new deployments but togglable via configuration on Dedicated/Private customers for two release cycles. Related: ENG-7421 (parity work), ENG-7550 (streaming stability incident follow-up), SUP-1987 (customer ticket reporting truncated function calls).

customer_impact: fixes cases where streaming responses could truncate tool/function call payloads, and improves compatibility for customers migrating from OpenAI APIs.
